newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda tribunal makes first genocide acquittal.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal makes first genocide acquittal.

text.p: A Rwandan tribunal has acquitted a suspect accused of genocide, the first to go free since trials began in December, a court official said on Thursday.
Felix Ndhegwa, an official at the court in the southwestern town of Gikongoro, told Reuters by telephone Israel Nemeyimana was freed by the court on Tuesday.
"There was no evidence and no witnesses to testify against him," Ndhegwa said.
Nemeyimana was accused of murder, an offence which comes into the second of four categories used to determine the weight of the crime under Rwanda's 1996 law on the 1994 genocide.
Ndhegwa said also on Tuesday in the Gikongoro court five other people were given life sentences for involvement in the genocide.
Trials began in December of some of the more than 90,000 people, a vast majority from the Hutu majority, accused of involvement in the mass slaughter and crammed into Rwanda's prisons.
An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates were killed in the three-month genocide by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs.
So far at least 11 death sentences have been handed out by tribunals in sessions across the tiny central African country.

Human rights groups have criticised the tribunals, saying most of those found guilty and sentenced to death had no defence lawyers. Rwandan authorities say most defendants at trials in Rwanda even before the genocide had no defence representation.
